title: His Stopping Distance
hook: Old Ninety is ahead. Your nose is close.
scene: Wind, morning, I-5 south, three lanes. A rogue semi with a dirty number that used to be ninety holds the right. You sit in the same lane, a car length off his trailer doors. At city speed that gap felt like plenty. At this number he cannot stop for you, and you just borrowed the only pavement he had. The left is open enough to leave or to drop back until you can count more than a car.
decision: You are a car length off his trailer at highway speed. Where do you sit?

options.text: Hold the car length — if he can roll, you can roll
options.result: His brake lamps come on for a dead van you cannot see. You have his leftover and no more. You borrowed a loaded trailer's stopping distance.

options.text: Tuck left and cruise beside the trailer so you are not behind him
options.result: You live in the place he cannot see. He starts a move that needs your lane. You are the car in the statistic again, at a higher number.

options.text: Drop back until you can count three or more, or pass once and clear
options.result: You give him pavement he can actually use. Or you pass once, all the way, and you do not sit on his door. Either way you stop borrowing his stop.

options.text: Close up so no one can cut in between you and the trailer
options.result: You erase the last of his margin to keep a hole closed. The next brake is still his. You made it yours.

debrief: A loaded trailer needs more than a car length at highway speed. You either dropped back or you passed and cleared. You took back the pavement you had borrowed.

source.psdp_skill: Skill eleven: highway driving – part two
source.teaching_target: Give large vehicles extra following distance at highway speed; do not sit a car length off a loaded trailer.
